A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and relocated content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments evaluating LLM response distributions and supervised calibration on WGM, OpinionQA and WVS, including demographic and generalization analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices and additionally reports detailed statistics for existing comparisons.

M1.justification: Both versions calibrate individual answer-choice probabilities using supervised regression and then renormalize distributions. The elicitation procedures and prompt templates are retained. V3's hyperparameter grid documents the existing approach rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both use the same 92 questions: 14 from WGM, 38 from OpinionQA and 40 from WVS, with unchanged demographic coverage. The held-out-dataset generalization scenario remains in v2 Appendix A.4 and v3 Appendix D.4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments. Base/SD prompting, CoT, five-shot prompting, log-probability elicitation and OLMo post-training variants remain evaluated with the same participating models.

E3.justification: The split proportions, metrics, model configurations, elicitation settings and few-shot design are retained. V3 explicitly specifies splitting by question and reporting test-set results; these clarify the existing protocol, consistent with v2's description of held-out test questions.

E4.justification: The CoT case study, training-size sensitivity, subgroup degradation, post-training comparison and out-of-domain analyses are retained. Several move into v3 Appendices A-C, D.4 and F; their relocation does not introduce or remove analyses.

E5.justification: V2 already reports paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction and repeated sampling. V3 Appendix G and Table 14 add explicit t-statistics, corrected p-values, the reported Bonferroni alpha of 0.000172, approximate average sample size of 237, and discussion of normality assumptions. No increase in runs is stated.

E6.justification: Existing performance-table values, significance bolding and plotted results are unchanged after matching relocated content. V3 adds previously unreported statistical result entries in Table 14. Figure 2's caption also changes the omitted-point denominator from 43/290 to 43/270, while retaining the same plot.

T1.justification: The opinion-alignment equation and regression formulation remain equivalent. Cardinality notation and the clarification of full examples do not introduce new mathematics. Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: SD prompting gives inconsistent improvements, calibration improves alignment by 16.3% on average, and 1-10 examples can suffice. Post-training conclusions survive in Appendix A despite their removal from the introduction's research-question summary.

C2.justification: V3's Limitations explicitly explains that predicting answer choices independently ignores correlations and may cause over-smoothing, loss of distributional structure and distortions. V2 describes independent prediction but does not articulate these specific risks. The principal interpretations of the empirical findings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds the exact calibration hyperparameter search grid in Appendix H, clearer split and example-unit descriptions, and model/software access links. Conversely, the code/data footnote replaces v2's named repository address with a promise of availability upon publication.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially narrows its literature coverage by removing the entire probabilistic-reasoning, LLM-regression and forecasting discussion and the broad applications paragraph, with their corresponding references. V3 sharpens its comparison with Meister et al. (2025) and adds primary WGM/WVS references and Smucker et al. (2007) on significance testing.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, methodological explanations and discussion undergo extensive condensation and rewriting. Post-training, CoT and few-shot sections move to appendices, and limitations are reorganized. Some cross-references remain stale, including Appendix A's reference to RQ5 after the introduction lists only four research questions.

P2.justification: The document substantially redistributes its displays: two plots and the CoT/few-shot tables move to appendices, tables share newly arranged pages, and prompt templates use smaller type. V3 adds statistical Table 14 and revises Figure 2's caption. Existing plot images are unchanged; Table 18 retains outdated result-table references.

improvement.justification: Section 3.6 and Appendices G-H make the unchanged experiments easier to assess and reproduce through clearer split descriptions, explicit statistical results and hyperparameter grids. The new calibration-specific limitations improve qualification of the findings. These provide a modest net improvement in transparency, tempered by less specific release information and stale cross-references introduced during reorganization.
